rationale: The clause permits deposit deductions without the template's written breach notice and cure period; clarify that process before signing.
Unbounded loss or liability and unilateral final assessment omit the template's reasonable deduction and written notice/cure safeguards.

The per-item cap is configurable in ITEM 10; allocation of excess repair costs and landlord responsibility for structural defects broadly match the template. Absence of a problem-free-period phrase in this isolated clause is not proof that the whole agreement omits it.
Tenant liability for every repair regardless of cause or amount contrasts with the capped minor-repair allocation and landlord-paid excess in the template.
Either party's general one-month exit right materially differs from the template's enumerated landlord termination triggers and breach-cure procedure.
An undefined notice period decided finally by the landlord gives materially different termination discretion from the template's specified events and written breach/cure process.
The clause allows subletting or assignment with landlord consent while the template's tenant covenant says not to assign or sublet; HDB approval implications remain outside this comparison.

The template fixes named occupiers but does not establish whether a 30-day guest becomes an occupier or justify an additional-rent or deposit rule; the selected clause alone cannot support a specific comparison.
A fixed S$10-per-day late charge differs from the template's 10% annual interest on unpaid rent after seven days.
The template's rent schedule does not determine whether separate agent reminder or document fees are permitted or already specified elsewhere; silence alone cannot establish a material difference.
The clause permits withholding disputed deductions without stating the template's written notice and fourteen-day opportunity to remedy a breach.
The emergency-repair exception allows work before written approval while the template requires prior written consent for repairs above the agreed cap.
Immediate termination for any breach and automatic deposit retention contrast with the template's written notice and fourteen-day cure condition for ordinary breaches.
The landlord's at-will owner-occupation exit after two months differs from the template's specified landlord termination grounds; the replacement-tenant burden also needs clarification.
Open-ended reasonable occupants do not identify the permitted occupiers as the template's schedule requires for the tenancy comparison.
Conditional subletting with landlord consent and possible higher charges materially differs from the template's tenant covenant not to assign or sublet.
Landlord-defined usual utility usage and final excess calculations replace the template's allocation of actual utility charges to the tenant.
General agent assistance and advice do not state a comparable operative payment or tenancy obligation in the indexed template sections.
The clause does not identify which party pays for particular repairs or any cost threshold, so the template's responsibility split cannot be reliably compared.
Broad any-amount deductions and an indefinite return after final determination omit the template's reasonable-breach deduction with written notice and cure process.
